title: Son of God
definition: Son of God refers to what Scripture reveals about the person, work, glory, or saving ministry of Jesus Christ.
summary: Son of God refers to what Scripture reveals about the person, work, glory, or saving ministry of Jesus Christ.
christFocus: This doctrine centers on Jesus Himself, showing His glory, His saving work, and His faithful heart toward sinners, sufferers, and disciples.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture reveals son of God so believers can behold the Savior as He truly is. This doctrine is not a side detail; it helps show why Jesus is worthy of trust, worship, obedience, and proclamation.

Every truth about Christ carries Gospel weight. His person and work answer the real condition of sinners: guilt, shame, alienation, weakness, death, and the need for reconciliation with God.

This doctrine draws the heart to Jesus rather than to religious performance. The believer does not merely learn about Christ but is called to come to Him, follow Him, and live from His grace by the Spirit's power.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People can speak of Jesus in vague ways while missing the saving truth Scripture gives. This doctrine helps keep the Church's faith centered on the real Christ, not a reduced version shaped by culture or preference.

For the rejected, ashamed, disabled, recovering, or weary believer, son of God shows that Christ is not distant from their need. He is sufficient, present, and mighty to save.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look to Christ according to this truth. Worship Him, trust His finished work, bring your weakness to Him, and ask the Holy Spirit to help you follow Him with faithfulness in ordinary life.
